title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.9021: R = 2^22 partition rows, pass 2 by 128, a 32-pair arrival loop and a halved doubling rate at kappa = 1.0002

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack of proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^125.9021 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). It builds on the 125.9022 crown (6a6cb91c, R = 2^21) (kappa = 1.0002 from the shipped hazard census, proof.md section 5.2, h = 0.000203 and p0 = 0.3902033, all unchanged; kaankolcu's 4595bad7 kernels with pass 2 storing -(W + T); pass 2 unrolled 128 times; arrival loop of 32 pairs; doubling recounted with rare-exit kernels and 3-instruction escape logic, surcharge 132 milli-units) with one change: the partition table doubled to R = 2^22 rows, so the arrival BFI writes 23 bits (bits 0..22 of K0 + 1 into bits 9..31 of the slot base, still one instruction at the same 1024-byte stride, 2^32-byte table), and the 2-cycle rate 1/(6R) halves to 2^-24.585 with the traversal and rare-entry rates. The ordinary step is unchanged at 99.515625 + 444.515625 + 31.015625 + 25391/2^20 = 575.0711 instructions; the declared run executes the shipped loops and arrival rows at exactly these counts. Rare exits charge 20 milli-units each and run the inline kernel's own instructions; the declared run enters all 1,167 exit stubs. Recovery probability is greater than 0.39000019 and therefore at least 0.39 (failure rows 1.0103e-7 < 1.1e-7). Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units, charged and included; nonuniform advice is zero. Exact ledger: S_ops = 1.0002*S0 = 2^126.7000179, phase 1 = 2^125.901830, hard extras = 2^112.575681, allowance = 2^112.186338, W_ledger = 2^125.9020777 < 2^125.9021; Markov ratio 0.0001680225 (certificate) and 0.00016813991 (experiment.py's float ledger), < 0.000203; certificate.py checks W^10000 < 1000^10000*2^1259021 and W^10000 > 1000^10000*2^1259020 exactly. No prior acceptance, review verdict or official score is a premise. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and the canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk (even-y key, per-trail anchor phases) on subgroups of y^2=x^3+7, with node routing and a long-trail trap test; kernels: Python limb ports of the field kernels against big integers, and the shipped unrolled loops (with their rare exits, on constructed inputs that enter every stub), emitter wrappers and arrival rows executed by an AArch64 interpreter (kernels/a64.py) against affine secp256k1, a bit-exact model and the exact canonical rule, with instruction counts and the ledger of proof.md recomputed. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
